verified_facts.claim: OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra reached their Preparedness Framework's 'Critical' threshold for cybersecurity capability—the first model to do so
verified_facts.finding: Multiple sources, including OpenAI's official safety overview, confirm that GPT-6 Astra reached the 'Critical' threshold for cybersecurity capability under OpenAI's Preparedness Framework. OpenAI explicitly states this is their first model to reach this level.

verified_facts.claim: METR forecast that 99% AI R&D automation arrives around 2032 based on coding-agent transcript analysis
verified_facts.finding: METR's model does predict 99% AI R&D automation around 2032, but it is NOT based on 'coding-agent transcript analysis.' The model is based on estimates of algorithmic efficiency growth (5x/year), compute scaling (2.6x/year through 2029), and current automation levels (25-50% as of January 2026). The claim mischaracterizes the methodology used in METR's forecast.

verified_facts.claim: METR's 2025 horizon projections for 1-4 hour tasks rely on only 14 samples
verified_facts.finding: The claim is confirmed by search results. According to The Beat's article, as of 2025, the METR plot showed frontier AI progress in the 1-4 hour horizon range, and there are only 14 samples with estimated task lengths in this range. This creates a small sample size problem for projections in this critical regime.

verified_facts.claim: 37% gap documented between AI lab benchmark scores and real-world deployment performance due to ambiguous requests, flaky APIs, rate limits, unexpected formats
verified_facts.finding: Multiple sources confirm a 37% gap between AI lab benchmark scores and real-world deployment performance. However, the specific causes listed in the claim (ambiguous requests, flaky APIs, rate limits, unexpected formats) are not mentioned or verified in any of the search results provided.

disputed_claims.claim: GPT-6 Astra proceeded to deployment with 'stronger safeguards' after crossing Critical cybersecurity threshold
disputed_claims.competing_accounts: OpenAI asserts safeguards were added; observer (journal author) notes safeguard details remain unspecified in public documentation and questions whether Critical threshold meaningfully constrained deployment

disputed_claims.claim: METR's horizon projections demonstrate robust exponential trends toward AI R&D automation
disputed_claims.competing_accounts: METR presents forecast derived from coding-agent transcripts; critic notes projections rely on only 14 samples, raising statistical robustness concerns

competing_frames.summary: Independent red-teaming of lab monitoring systems provides necessary verification of safety claims that internal assessments cannot supply

competing_frames.proponents: Observer analysis across journals J12, J13, J24
competing_frames.summary: Labs ship agentic capabilities faster than external evals and monitoring can verify their safety, creating widening gap between deployment speed and verification maturity
Labs can self-regulate through responsible scaling policies and calls for shared standards while continuing deployment
Lab-reported benchmark scores do not reliably predict real-world performance due to distribution shift, small sample sizes, and deployment environment differences
